"""
lru_ttl_cache.py
================

A complete, production-ready Python module implementing:

1. :class:`LRUTTLCache` - A Least Recently Used (LRU) cache with
   Time-To-Live (TTL) expiry per entry.
2. :class:`ThreadSafeLRUTTLCache` - A thin, thread-safe wrapper around
   :class:`LRUTTLCache` using :mod:`threading.RLock`.
3. A comprehensive :mod:`pytest` test suite located at the bottom of
   this file (guarded by ``if __name__ == "__main__":`` so it can be
   executed directly or imported by pytest).

The implementation is intentionally dependency-free (standard library
only) so it can be dropped into any project without additional
installation steps.

Design notes
------------
* **Ordering** – We keep an ``collections.OrderedDict`` where the *most
  recently used* items are moved to the end. The *least recently used*
  item is therefore always at the beginning (index 0) and can be evicted
  in O(1) time when the cache exceeds ``maxsize``.
* **TTL** – Each entry stores an absolute expiry timestamp
  (``time.monotonic() + ttl``). On every access we check whether the
  current time has passed the expiry; if so the entry is treated as
  missing and removed lazily.
* **Thread safety** – The non-thread-safe core assumes the caller
  serialises access. The wrapper serialises every public method with a
  re-entrant lock so the same thread can safely call nested methods
  (e.g. ``get_or_set`` calling ``get`` then ``set``).
* **Complexity** – All public operations are O(1) average time and
  O(N) space where N is ``maxsize``.

Example usage
-------------

>>> from lru_ttl_cache import LRUTTLCache, ThreadSafeLRUTTLCache
>>> import time
>>>
>>> # Basic non-thread-safe cache, max 3 items, 2 second TTL
>>> cache = LRUTTLCache(maxsize=3, default_ttl=2.0)
>>> cache.set("a", 1)
>>> cache.get("a")
1
>>> time.sleep(2.1)
